Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Orlena usually hope their child will grow to embody light, mountain of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It represents the spiritual journey towards enlightenment and the notion that we can always seek God's light to navigate through life's challenges and uncertainties.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Orlena is a name derived from the Old Slavic word "orlo," meaning eagle. In Christian tradition, this name represents the strength and courage of the eagle, symbolizing one who soars above the worldly distractions and remains focused on the spiritual journey towards God.

historical_references.reference: According to local legend, Orlena was a Christian martyr in ancient Greece who was tortured and killed for her faith during the reign of Emperor Nero in the 1st century AD.

Orlena is also mentioned in medieval Christian hagiography as a legendary princess who converted her pagan father to Christianity and was martyred for her faith during the late 12th or early 13th century in Eastern Europe.
